once.prompt: Marc needs the Belmara rate base for the BPUC by Friday 30 October. Work out what we have invested in plant, pipes and treatment, net of depreciation, at the 31 December 2026 test year end; show that the additions were prudent and are used and useful; and draft the rate base schedules in the 2025 structure, a prudence and used-and-useful memo, and a few slides for the working session with BPUC staff on 4 November. Attached: the 2025 rate base schedules and the BPUC post-test-year schedule.

reads.res: Schedules RB-1 to RB-5; rate base $776.9M at 31 December 2024, allowed in full. The structure the BPUC accepted
38 projects, $214.6M, claimed in service by 31 December 2026 · update due 13 November
Belmara plant in service $1,489.7M gross, $414.5M accumulated depreciation at 30 September, in five classes
$287.6M in CWIP · WIN approvals, awards and change orders for every addition above $2.5M
Seven of the 38 post-test-year projects now dated 2027, $41.3M · two of the 31 on track have no row
Marc: schedules by 30 October, approved rates · Plant Accounting: nine projects in service since May to July still in CWIP, $6.8M
Plant enters rate base only in service at the test year end · approved depreciation rates until a new order · additions above $2.5M need a prudence record

questions.title: Nine projects are in service but still booked to CWIP ($6.8M): do they count?
questions.text: Plant Accounting says nine Belmara projects went into service between May and July, with certificates on file, but they stay in CWIP until the 6 November close. The order keeps CWIP out of rate base, but plant in service at the test year end counts.

tiles.t: Leave them in CWIP, as booked today
tiles.s: $6.8M lower; they move on 6 November anyway

tiles.t: Ask me again before the schedules

questions.title: The seven post-test-year projects now dated 2027: how do the schedules treat them?
questions.text: The 12 October in-service file moves seven of the 38 into 2027 ($41.3M). The order removes anything not in service by 31 December, and the update is due 13 November. Only one project manager has confirmed so far.

tiles.t: Take them out now and list them for the next case
Out of the total, on a separate at-risk list

tiles.s: Only if the PMs correct the dates

nodes.title: State plant in service and depreciation by class
nodes.purpose: What Belmara has invested in plant, pipes and treatment, and what is left after depreciation.
nodes.how: Gross plant in service and accumulated depreciation by class at 30 September, from the fixed-asset ledger, at the approved depreciation rates; reconciled to the 2025 schedules.
nodes.check: Classes sum to the fixed-asset ledger; depreciation at the approved rates.

nodes.title: Test what is used and useful at 31 December
nodes.purpose: Which additions are in service at the test year end, and which are not.
nodes.how: The 38 post-test-year projects against the 12 October in-service file and the project managers’ replies; completed construction still in CWIP; the CWIP the order keeps out.
nodes.check: Every project is in, out or held, with the reason.

nodes.title: Roll the rate base forward from the 2025 order
nodes.purpose: From $776.9M at the 2024 test year end to 31 December 2026.
nodes.how: Additions and depreciation since the 2024 test year, the fourth-quarter additions and depreciation, then contributions, deferred taxes, advances, cash working capital and materials, in the RB-1 to RB-5 structure.
nodes.check: The roll-forward ties back to the $776.9M allowed and forward to the ledger.

nodes.title: Confirm how the nine completed projects in CWIP are treated
nodes.purpose: Stops here and asks you before the prudence review and the schedules.
nodes.how: Plant Accounting has not moved the nine yet. The schedules and the memo rest on how they are treated, and only you can confirm it.
nodes.check: Your answer is recorded on the plan before anything after it runs.

nodes.title: Check the prudence record of the major additions
nodes.purpose: Whether each addition above $2.5M can show it was prudently incurred.
nodes.how: For the twelve largest fourth-quarter additions: the WIN approval and its level, the business case, the award (bids, or a sole-source justification), and every change order with its approval.
nodes.check: Every addition has a complete record, or its gap is named.

nodes.title: What to present, and how
nodes.purpose: One rate base to present, with what it trades off.
nodes.how: Weigh presenting the seven out against keeping all 38 as filed, or holding for the close and the confirmations; state the trade-off and every caveat that reached it.
nodes.check: The recommendation names its remaining caveats and the alternatives it rejected.

nodes.title: Draft the schedules, the memo and the slides
nodes.how: Schedules RB-1 to RB-5 on the 2025 structure; a prudence and used-and-useful memo; a short deck for the 4 November session. Every figure linked to the step that produced it.
draws: Template: Belmara rate base schedules, 2025 case

four.how: Takes the nine out of plant in service and re-reads the rate base; shares steps 1 to 3.

summary: The rate base is $1,072.6M at 31 December 2026, $295.7M (38.1%) above the $776.9M allowed in 2025. Net plant rises to $1,246.0M with the fourth-quarter additions; contributions, deferred taxes and advances take off $192.9M, and cash working capital and materials add $19.5M.

At the allowed return that is about $31.3M a year more revenue requirement. Marc asked for the approved depreciation rates: the 2026 study proposes 2.6% against 2.4%, which would take $2.4M off the rate base and add the same a year to depreciation expense. It is not filed.

summary: Ten of the twelve largest additions ($141.7M) have a complete prudence record; two, $34.1M together, have gaps. Each of the ten has its WIN approval at the right level, a business case, a competitive award and change orders approved at their level.

The two: PFAS GAC Install, Brookmere ($28.94M), where amendment CO-645-001 ($868,000) and change order CO-645-002 ($351,000) were approved without the cost comparison the policy asks for above $250,000; and Booster Station Upgrade, Belmara Central ($5.20M), where the $675,000 electrical and controls package (PO-467906-03) was placed sole source without the justification the policy requires.
